test.explain: A trial dose by lumbar puncture checks that the patient actually benefits before committing to surgery.

test.q: Which drug do Gliadel wafers release into the cavity left after brain tumor surgery?
choices: Carmustine
Methotrexate
Baclofen
Ziconotide
test.explain: Gliadel wafers are biodegradable polymer discs loaded with carmustine. Methotrexate is given into the ventricles via an Ommaya reservoir, not by wafer.

test.q: Which set lists the drugs approved in the US for chronic intrathecal pump infusion?
choices: Morphine, ziconotide and baclofen
Methotrexate, ziconotide and insulin
Insulin, heparin and morphine
Fentanyl, baclofen and carmustine
test.explain: Morphine, ziconotide and baclofen are the approved agents for chronic intrathecal pump infusion. Insulin and carmustine are delivered by other routes.

test.q: Release from a matrix implant often falls in proportion to the square root of time, as described by the ___ model.
test.explain: In a matrix, the diffusion path lengthens as drug near the surface leaves, so release slows with the square root of time (Higuchi).

test.q: An automated insulin delivery system links an insulin pump to a continuous glucose ___.
test.explain: The continuous glucose monitor feeds readings to the pump, which adjusts insulin automatically.

test.q: What term describes delivery of a drug directly into the cerebrospinal fluid around the spinal cord?
test.explain: Intrathecal means into the CSF-filled space around the spinal cord, bypassing the blood-brain barrier.

kidTest.q: What does a medicine implant do?
choices: Cleans your blood
Lets out medicine slowly
Measures your temperature
kidTest.explain: An implant slowly lets out a little medicine each day, like a dripping sponge.

kidTest.q: Where can a medicine pump sit inside the body?
choices: Under the belly skin
Inside the stomach itself
Inside the bones of the leg
kidTest.explain: Implanted pumps sit under the skin of the belly.

kidTest.q: Intrathecal delivery sends medicine into the:
choices: Air spaces deep inside the lungs
Tear film covering the eyes
Fluid around the spinal cord
kidTest.explain: Intrathecal means into the fluid around the spinal cord.

kidTest.q: Why does a very small amount of intrathecal medicine work?
choices: It goes right where it is needed
It is mixed with extra sugar
It stays in the stomach longer
kidTest.explain: It skips the long trip through the body and lands right where it is needed.

kidTest.q: A small machine that pushes out tiny drops of medicine is a p _ _ _.
kidTest.explain: A pump pushes out medicine on a schedule.

advancedTest.q: A patient with a gas-propellant constant-flow intrathecal pump develops a high fever. What happens to delivery?
choices: It rises as warmer propellant exerts more pressure
It halts as the pump battery overheats and fails
It holds steady because the capillary fixes it
It falls as the warmed drug thickens in the tube
advancedTest.explain: Vapour pressure of the propellant rises with temperature, increasing the pressure driving flow through the capillary. The capillary sets resistance, not a flow independent of pressure, and these pumps have no battery.

advancedTest.q: Why does intrathecal morphine, but not intrathecal fentanyl, cause respiratory depression hours after a bolus?
choices: It is stored in epidural fat and released later
It enters blood fast and depresses the lungs directly
It is converted in CSF into a stronger metabolite
It lingers in CSF and drifts up to the brainstem
advancedTest.explain: Hydrophilic morphine has long CSF residence and spreads rostrally to brainstem respiratory centres. Lipophilic fentanyl is the one that moves quickly into epidural fat and blood, acting segmentally.

advancedTest.q: The core of a PLGA implant degrades faster than its surface. The best explanation is:
choices: Body heat is concentrated at the implant center
Tissue enzymes reach the center faster than water
Drug crystals coat and shield the outer surface
Trapped acidic breakdown products speed hydrolysis
advancedTest.explain: In bulk erosion, lactic and glycolic acid oligomers accumulate inside and autocatalyze ester hydrolysis, while at the surface they diffuse away.

advancedTest.q: A patient on long-term intrathecal morphine slowly loses pain relief, then develops progressive leg weakness. The most likely cause is:
choices: Opioid tolerance from receptor downregulation
Rostral spread causing brainstem depression
An inflammatory mass at the catheter tip
Withdrawal caused by sudden pump failure
advancedTest.explain: Gradual loss of efficacy followed by new neurological deficit is the classic picture of a catheter-tip granuloma compressing the cord. Tolerance explains lost relief but not weakness.
